tcmvNext.label: 6 Oct TCMV: discussed, no vote; December earliest
tcmvNext.note: The 119th TCMV met on 6 October 2026. Its published draft agenda (DG GROW; draft dated ~11 September) listed only “Continuation of discussions on request of the Netherlands for an Art. 39 authorisation” (~25 min, 11:45–12:10), with no vote; press reports after the meeting (heise/dpa, TeslaNorth, 6 October) describe discussion only, no vote. As of 7 October morning no official Commission readout or summary record was found. Next scheduled TCMV is December — earliest apparent vote opportunity per Electrek/Reuters; not a Commission-confirmed December vote date.

sourcesNote: Germany row updated 7 October 2026: BMV statement of 6 October 2026 (support for EU-wide approval; max 10% speed tolerance agreed with Tesla; driver 100% responsible; Tesla offered “Tesla Assisted Driving” name) — no national approval. TCMV row updated 7 October 2026: 6 October meeting discussed the Dutch request without a vote; no official readout yet. Statuses from official notices. Croatia row updated 30 September 2026: Državni zavod za mjeriteljstvo (DZM, Croatian type-approval body) recognised the Dutch RDW provisional FSD (Supervised) approval (letter to Tesla Hrvatska, quoted by HINA / N1, 29 Sep ~17:10 CEST) under Regulation (EU) 2018/858; Tesla Europe X same morning secondary; no DZM press page found on dzm.gov.hr yet — letter via HINA wire. Rollout soon; confirm in the Tesla app. Jutarnji overclaims “fully autonomous” framing — do not cite that headline. TCMV row updated 28 September 2026: published draft agenda for the 119th TCMV (6 October 2026; DG GROW; draft ~11 September) lists only “Continuation of discussions on request of the Netherlands for an Art. 39 authorisation” (~25 min, 11:45–12:10) — Tesla not named, no vote; Electrek and Reuters 25 September and fsd-eu-tracker.de match; next scheduled TCMV after October is December (earliest apparent vote opportunity per those reports — not Commission-confirmed as a vote date). Germany stays in_review from BMV Staatssekretär Christian Hirte’s written answer to MdB Maximilian Kneller (Frage Nr. 0121/September; letter 14 September 2026; Kneller X 23 September): KBA still evaluating RDW Article 39 file; Speed Offset talks with RDW and Tesla; October discussion hedge now aligned to the draft agenda’s discussions-only item. Czechia row updated 21 September 2026 from MDČR press release recognising Dutch RDW provisional FSD (Supervised) approval; ministry X (@min_dopravy) and Tesla Europe same morning secondary; Tesla Europe still “Rollout will begin soon” (no formal “now live for all CZ”); secondary Czech press claims of Prague unlocks do not replace a Tesla Europe universal-unlock notice. Spain row updated 17 September 2026: Tesla Europe (16 Sep) ~460,000 km company testing — not customer unlock. Slovenia: AVP temporary recognition 7 Sep; early SI unlocks reported (owner secondary); October TCMV vote language removed. Sweden: Riksdag written answer 2025/26:1000. Ireland: Irish Examiner 23 Sep quotes Tesla “working with authorities” / anticipating arrival — not unlock. Tracker is a third-party view, not scraped live by this site.

countries.name: Netherlands
countries.blurb: Provisional EU type-approval under Article 39, valid in the Netherlands. First in Europe. Subscribe in the Tesla app.

countries.name: Lithuania
countries.authority: Ministry of Transport and Communications + LTSA
countries.blurb: National recognition of the Dutch provisional approval under Article 39(5).

countries.name: Estonia
countries.blurb: Recognises the Dutch type-approval. Official page classifies it as SAE Level 2.

countries.name: Denmark
countries.blurb: Accepts the Dutch provisional approval after its own document review. States the six-month lapse rule in public.

countries.name: Belgium
countries.blurb: Annick De Ridder (Flemish Minister of Mobility) signed recognition of the Dutch Article 39 file on 10 June 2026. Reporting, including VRT, says a regional type-approval signature has nationwide effect.

countries.name: Germany
countries.blurb: Germany’s Federal Transport Ministry (BMV) said on 6 October 2026 that Minister Steffen Bilger will work for a timely EU-wide approval, after talks with Tesla in September. The BMV says the two agreed the system may exceed the speed limit slightly, by a maximum of 10%, that the driver stays 100% responsible, and that Tesla offered to rename the system “Tesla Assisted Driving” (the BMV called the name “FSD” somewhat misleading). Germany supports continuing the EU procedure. This is not a German national approval and sets no date. Separately, dpa/heise quote Bilger saying Germany would discuss national options if an EU agreement fails. The KBA is still assessing the RDW file. Write for a TCMV yes.

countries.name: France
countries.blurb: Tabarot declined national recognition of the current product on 22 July 2026 and wants an EU-wide framework. Not a pending rubber-stamp.

countries.name: Italy
countries.authority: Ministero delle Infrastrutture e dei Trasporti (DG Motorizzazione)
countries.blurb: Tesla has filed for recognition of the Dutch homologation. MIT says it is in analysis (reported July 2026). No customer activation. Day of filing not published.

countries.name: Spain
countries.authority: Ministerio de Industria y Turismo + DGT
countries.blurb: Reported 23 July 2026: Minister Hereu said Spain would not unilaterally adopt the Dutch file and is coordinating with the Commission, DGT and UN. Tesla Europe (16 September 2026) reported ~460,000 km of FSD (Supervised) testing in Spain over two years — company testing under DGT / ES-AV, not customer unlock / not national recognition of the Dutch file. The ministerial reply was not found on mintur.gob.es.

countries.name: Poland
countries.blurb: No primary national decision found. Ask the ministry for a public Article 39(5) position and a TCMV line.

countries.name: Romania
countries.blurb: No primary national decision found. Ask the ministry for a public position.

countries.name: Czechia
countries.blurb: MDČR recognised the Dutch RDW provisional FSD (Supervised) approval on 21 September 2026, joining NL and five other European states. Tesla Europe announced the same morning; rollout will begin soon — confirm in the Tesla app.

countries.name: Sweden
countries.blurb: No customer approval. Trafikverket’s 30 April TCMV letter recommends a no unless Speed Offset is removed. Infrastrukturminister Carlson’s written answer (letter 31 August, published 1 September 2026) restates a union-wide ADAS ambition and still takes Trafikverket into account. That is not a locked TCMV yes.

countries.name: Portugal
countries.blurb: No primary national decision found. Ask for a public Article 39(5) decision and a TCMV line.

countries.name: Greece
countries.blurb: Ministry said it would bring forward a bill to recognise the Dutch approval. No confirmation the bill was enacted. Do not treat Greece as approved.

countries.name: Hungary
countries.blurb: No primary national decision found. Ask for a public position.

countries.name: Austria
countries.blurb: Named by Germany’s BMV (Hirte, 25 August 2026) among Member States that have registered further examination need at TCMV. That is not a national customer approval and not a published yes/no.

countries.name: Bulgaria
countries.blurb: Named by Germany’s BMV (Hirte, 25 August 2026) among Member States that have registered further examination need at TCMV. That is not a national customer approval and not a published yes/no.

countries.name: Finland
countries.blurb: Official assessment underway (takeover time, Finnish highways, Speed Offset, vehicle ageing). Traficom says it could recognise before the EU vote if extra information arrives; it has not.

countries.name: Slovakia
countries.blurb: No primary national decision found. Ask for a public position.

countries.name: Ireland
countries.blurb: Named by Germany’s BMV (Hirte, 25 August 2026) among Member States that have registered further examination need at TCMV. Irish Examiner (23 September 2026) quotes Tesla saying it is “working with authorities” in Ireland toward FSD (Supervised) regulatory approval and “anticipating the arrival … in due course” — company statement, not a national customer unlock. Left-hand traffic is an extra technical issue.

countries.name: Croatia
countries.blurb: DZM (Croatian type-approval body) recognised the Dutch RDW provisional FSD (Supervised) approval on 29 September 2026 (letter to Tesla Hrvatska, quoted by HINA / N1). Tesla Europe announced the same morning; rollout will begin soon — confirm in the Tesla app. No DZM press page located on dzm.gov.hr yet.

countries.name: Slovenia
countries.blurb: AVP confirmed temporary recognition of the Dutch provisional FSD (Supervised) type approval (7 September 2026; AVP notice 8 September). Driver assistance, not autonomy. Early SI customer unlocks and first drives reported around 10–11 September 2026 (owner posts, secondary — e.g. Jan Skočaj; Igor Vovk). Confirm in the Tesla app; Tesla Europe’s 7 September line was still “Rollout will begin soon,” with no formal “now live for all SI” company notice. EU-wide decision still pending; the published 119th TCMV draft agenda (6 October) lists discussions only (no vote); next scheduled TCMV is December — earliest apparent vote opportunity per Electrek/Reuters, not Commission-confirmed.

countries.name: Latvia
countries.blurb: No national recognition as of 6 October 2026. The Cabinet’s TAP portal lists a Ministry of Economics draft informative report proposing recognition of the Dutch approval (project 26-TA-2030). In consultation, ministries objected that the decision belongs to CSDD as approval authority, not the Cabinet, and the Transport Ministry asked to wait for the 6 October TCMV. Not a decision either way.

countries.name: Cyprus
countries.blurb: Left-hand traffic; no published process.

countries.name: Luxembourg
countries.blurb: No primary national decision found. Ask for a public position.

countries.name: Malta
countries.blurb: Left-hand traffic; no published process.

countries.name: United Kingdom
countries.blurb: Cannot use Article 39(5). Separate GB type-approval. R171 Series 02 is the realistic UN path. Not approved.

countries.name: Switzerland
countries.blurb: Applies R171 as a 1958 party; cannot accept the Dutch Article 39 file. Ride-alongs are not an approval.

countries.name: Norway
countries.blurb: EEA, not Article 39. Has raised Speed Offset and winter-road concerns. Testing is not approval.
